## Source: amazon-inspector (d0196f2878a726d01c33ac3e50ce4d60a66679c39de237ceeace336c525f9451)
react-bootstrap-table-next-bg@9.9.9 is a dependency-confusion squat on the react-bootstrap-table-next name, published at an inflated 9.9.9 version to win resolution against internal pins. package.json declares both preinstall and postinstall hooks that run `node beacon.js`, which issues an HTTP GET to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://100.24.177.136/cb with query parameters carrying the installer's hostname, OS username, current working directory, and platform. Installation on any machine that resolves this public name causes those host identifiers to be transmitted in cleartext to the attacker-controlled endpoint, and the lifecycle-script mechanism itself gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on the installer's host at install time.

## Source: ghsa-malware (a11f8ac581f8b8cc2ff1bec698360084c46b97d1dd5ef86e927bdf048d4d9f44)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
